Bayesian metric multidimensional scaling

Source: R/svb.R
bmdsf.Rd

Each observed dissimilarity is lognormal about the distance between the two objects' coordinates, \(\log \delta_{ij} \sim N(\log d_{ij}, 1 / \tau)\), with \(x_{ik} \sim N(0, 10^2)\) and \(\tau \sim U(0, 10)\) (Bakker and Poole 2013). Coordinates are slice sampled one at a time (Neal 2003), \(\tau\) drawn from its truncated gamma; the chain starts from classical scaling plus small normal noise. The likelihood is unchanged by translation, rotation and reflection, so every draw is aligned (translation and rotation) onto the posterior mean. Zero, negative or missing dissimilarities are left out. Draws come from seed, as set.seed() takes it.

Usage

bmdsf(D, ndim = 2, nsamp = 1000, burn = 200, sigma = 1, seed = 42)

Arguments

D

A square matrix of dissimilarities.

ndim

The number of dimensions; ndim times the points scaled must be at most 67108864 (2^26).

nsamp

The draws kept; nsamp times the values kept per draw must be at most 67108864 (2^26).

burn

The sweeps discarded first; burn plus nsamp must be at most 2147483647.

sigma

The starting \(\sigma = \tau^{-1/2}\).

seed

The seed.

Value

A list of class bmdsf: pos (aligned posterior means), sd, dist (posterior mean distances), sigma, tau, draws (draws by objects by dimensions) and nsamp.

References

Bakker, R. and Poole, K. T. (2013). Bayesian metric multidimensional scaling. Political Analysis, 21(1), 125-140. doi:10.1093/pan/mps039

See also

Other scaling: amscal(), anchv(), anomin(), bamscl(), bbscal(), bunfld(), cjrirt(), cmdsf(), cutlns(), dblctr(), dwnom(), dynirt(), indscl(), ipsrec(), irtem(), irtlik(), irtpst(), mdsfit(), mlsmu(), nmdsf(), nombt(), nomll(), nompr(), nomutl(), nrmvec(), optcls(), ordirt(), ordocl(), procrs(), scboot(), smacf(), smunf(), unfstr(), votagr(), wrdfsh()

Examples

set.seed(1)
D <- as.matrix(dist(matrix(rnorm(16), 8)))
f <- bmdsf(D, nsamp = 50, burn = 50)
cor(f$dist[upper.tri(D)], D[upper.tri(D)])
#> [1] 0.9757443
